summary: Every legal input is the canonical Roman representation of an integer from 1 through 3,999 and has at most 15 symbols, so the source domain is too narrow for honest runtime scaling.

workload_bound.source_constraint: The source contract requires 1 <= |s| <= 15 and guarantees a valid numeral representing a value in [1, 3999].

replacement_checks.evidence: The solution performs one constant-work iteration per symbol, uses only a fixed seven-symbol mapping and scalar state, and therefore executes at most 15 iterations on the legal domain.

An independent digit-place encoder generates the canonical numeral for every integer from 1 through 3,999 and verifies both app-local and immutable native decoders, while the candidate is checked separately through the same complete domain.
